item.title: Learning Chmod Permissions in 30 Seconds
item.description:
Scary about “drwxr-xr-x”?

Don’t worry, in 30 seconds you’ll be able to read it!

Chmod always contains three groups, the first is (u)ser, then (g)roup and finally (o)ther (public)

-|rw-|r--|r-x
 | 1 | 2 | 3
 | u | g | o
  1. (u)ser: user can (r)ead and (w)rite
  2. (g)roup: user in this same group can (r)ead.
  3. (o)thers/public: can (r)ead and e(x)ecute.
U = User (1)
G = Group (2)
O = Other (Public) (3)

R = Read
W = Write
X = Execute

Give permisions:

chmod ugo+rwx hey.txt

item.title: Systemd Without Root and with Instances
item.description:
A user Systemd service should be placed in ~/.config/systemd/user/ directory if you want to have full ownership as normal user. Create it if it doesn’t exist.

mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user/

Create a systemd service unit file under the directory.
